title: Consolidated sample apps and ergonomic patterns for SDK retries & streaming
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Produce a small, opinionated set of sample applications and short cookbook patterns that demonstrate best-practice SDK usage for retries, streaming ergonomics, and cross-language examples (Next.js, FastAPI, Go HTTP server, and CLI). These artifacts should reduce onboarding time for engineers integrating Redwood SDKs and provide canonical patterns for production-grade behavior: idempotency, backoff strategies, reconnect handling for streaming, and token/connection resource hygiene.

Scope:
- 4 runnable sample apps (Next.js, FastAPI async, Go net/http streaming endpoints, and a CLI tool) with README integration steps.
- SDK helper snippets for: exponential/backoff jitter, idempotency keys, cancellation semantics, reconnect/resume for streaming, and memory-safe KV cache usage in long-lived servers.
- Tests + CI that exercise retries and streaming failure modes (mock server and recorded fixtures).
- Short developer guide (1-2 pages) with recommended defaults per language and migration notes for existing customers.

Acceptance criteria:
- Each sample app starts from a one-command dev flow (yarn/dev, uvicorn, go run, or bin/cli) and demonstrates streaming + graceful retry behavior.
- Example code uses the official Redwood SDK idioms (request/response models, streaming iterators) and shows how to set retry policy in a single place.
- Performance guidance section with trade-offs for batching vs latency.
- PR with code, READMEs, and a short demo video attached; internal docs linked from Console 'Get Started' guidelines.

Non-goals: full production readiness for every edge-case (we focus on pragmatic, easily auditable patterns).
